newsitem.title: SPAIN: RALLYING-SUBARU BATTLES MITSUBISHI FOR WORLD RALLY TITLE.
newsitem.headline: RALLYING-SUBARU BATTLES MITSUBISHI FOR WORLD RALLY TITLE.

text.p: Subaru will be looking to even the score with rivals Mitsubishi and their new world champion Tommi Makinen when the world rallying championship manfacturers' title is decided in Spain next week.
The Catalonia Rally, which starts on Monday, is the only round of this year's championship held entirely on asphalt roads and threatens to expose a hole in Mitsubishi's armour.

"Most of the stages are very driveable -- sometimes fast, with nice bends -- but it will be the most difficult rally of the year to win," said Makinen, aware his team was off the pace on the handful of asphalt stages in the penultimate round in San Remo.
Makinen faces an additional handicap -- co-driver Seppo Harjanne was injured in their accident in San Remo and he has a new navigator, fellow Finn Juha Repo, for the first time in seven years.

Subaru, who hold a 33-point lead over Mitsubishi in the manufacturers' title race, will take three cars into the deciding three-day rally driven by 1995 world champion Colin McRae, Italian asphalt specialist Piero Liatti and Swede Kenneth Eriksson.
McRae is keen to even the score with Spanish Ford driver Carlos Sainz after he was forced to follow team orders in Spain last year to let Sainz win, when they both drove for Subaru.

"It would be nice to put it all to rest -- the doubt whether Carlos could have won without team orders -- but I've got some brownie points after winning San Remo and it would be nice to get some more," the Briton said.
He predicted the factory Fords of Sainz and Belgian Bruno Thiry would set the pace in the 1,368-km rally but tyre choice and unpredictable weather could easily dictate the outcome.
